items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I think it was Paul West, the bass player in New York, and Frank Capp. You guys will accompany the singer

ctx.x: Well I’ll tell you how it all started. I used to be — Steve Allen was my friend. I was friends with Steve in the early 40s, late 40s. He became my friend then he became a big fan of mine, you know. And when he got his TV show he got me as a guest all the time, I was a guest a lot. And we were doing the show in California and I did his show with them and one of the producers, he loved me. He loved my dumb sense of humor, because I’m not a comedian but I’ve got the wit sort of like Steve’s. Steve loved me because,…

they said, “Okay we want you, it’s your job, but Steve Allen had a nine piece orchestra, we’ll give you a nine piece orchestra.” I said, “I don’t want it.” They said, “Well what do you mean?” I said, “You mean they give me a big band because we’re opposite Johnny Carson? Or opposite Elliot Lawrence who was with Les Crane — those shows at that time they all had 16 piece bands. And to me a 16 piece band — give me a sextet. I said sextet? Can you make it with a sextet? You see working with Steve Allen, of course I…

in at Letter D, the ending.” Play the intro — the singer never knew we never played the middle. We’d never do it. So that’s what I learned. So I did that for my TV shows, and then, you know it was, it just came naturally to me because the harder part got later on. See all the talent we had for the first maybe two or three weeks, and that’s why Regis, in last, where all the talent that already were booked for Steve Allen. And Steve was a big jazz fan so he’d have Sarah Vaughan, Stan Getz, Oscar Peterson, Count…
